note: STING model-authoring baseline. Corporate default; project override at <project>/_BIM_COORD/project_baseline.json, which wins by name. Material NAMES are load-bearing: the compound take-off infers brick vs block vs RC from them, and the finish classifier recognises tiling from them. Renaming a material here without checking those two is how a schedule goes quiet. Levels are deliberately EMPTY - level names and elevations are project decisions, so put them in the project override rather than auditing every model against someone else's storey heights.

materials.name: Concrete C25
materials.purpose: General structural concrete - slabs, columns, foundations

materials.name: Concrete C30
materials.purpose: Higher-grade structural concrete - RC walls, transfer elements

materials.name: Burnt Clay Brick
materials.purpose: Brick masonry - the take-off reads 'brick' from this name

materials.name: Hollow Concrete Block 200mm
materials.purpose: Block masonry - the take-off falls to block when the name is not brick

materials.name: Cement Plaster
materials.purpose: Render / plaster coat; the painted area is derived from it

materials.name: Cement Screed
materials.purpose: Floor screed under a tiled or applied finish

materials.name: Ceramic Tile
materials.purpose: Floor and wall tiling - recognised as tiling by the finish classifier

materials.name: Porcelain Tile
materials.purpose: Large-format tiling; carries a higher adhesive coverage

materials.name: Reinforcement Steel
materials.purpose: Rebar - reported in kg from the concrete volume

materials.name: Timber Formwork
materials.purpose: Sawn formwork, measured by contact area

materials.name: Corrugated Iron Sheet
materials.purpose: Sheet roof covering - the supplier rule converts it per sheet

wallTypes.name: STING Blockwork 200 - Plastered Both Faces
wallTypes.purpose: Standard internal / external block wall, plastered and painted both sides

wallTypes.name: STING Blockwork 200 - Tiled Wet Area
wallTypes.purpose: Bathroom / kitchen wall: plastered outside, tiled inside. The tiled face is measured as tiling and is NOT painted

wallTypes.name: STING Brickwork 230 - Plastered Both Faces
wallTypes.purpose: Burnt clay brick wall - the take-off reads 'brick' and counts bricks, not blocks

wallTypes.name: STING RC Wall 200
wallTypes.purpose: Reinforced concrete wall - decomposes to concrete, rebar and formwork to both faces

floorTypes.name: STING RC Slab 150 - Ceramic Tiled
floorTypes.purpose: Suspended slab with a tiled finish. The tile LAYER is what makes floor tiling measurable

floorTypes.name: STING RC Slab 200 - Porcelain Tiled
floorTypes.purpose: Heavier slab with large-format porcelain; adhesive coverage is higher than ceramic

floorTypes.name: STING RC Slab 150 - Screed Only
floorTypes.purpose: Slab left screeded, finish applied later or scheduled on the room

floorTypes.name: STING Ground Slab 150 on Blinding
floorTypes.purpose: Ground-bearing slab; the blinding is unreinforced by definition

roofTypes.name: STING RC Flat Roof 225
roofTypes.purpose: Concrete flat roof. The EXPLICIT concrete material is what lets it decompose to concrete, rebar and formwork - an unnamed roof material is treated as unknown, never as concrete

roofTypes.name: STING Sheet Roof - Corrugated IT4 G28
roofTypes.purpose: Sheet covering. The type NAME carries the supplier rule's patterns (sheet / corrugat / it4 / g28) so it converts to a sheet count

roofTypes.name: STING Tiled Roof - Clay Tile
roofTypes.purpose: Tiled covering; the name carries the roof-tile rule's patterns

ceilingTypes.name: STING Suspended Gypsum Ceiling
ceilingTypes.purpose: Plasterboard ceiling on a concealed grid

familyExpectations.guidance: Load a concrete column family and name its types so the material reads as concrete - the take-off decides column decomposition from the material, not the family name.
Load a foundation family. Pads and strips shutter on their SIDES only because they bear on the ground; blinding carries no rebar.
Load a concrete beam family; steel framing is left on the composite line rather than decomposed.
Doors are bought and belong in the schedule. They need a RATE keyed by type name in _BIM_COORD/commodity_rates.csv - the export names the exact key for every unpriced one.
As doors: present in the schedule, priced by type name in the project rate card.
